note: SCB's SNI 47.52 series decelerated from +9.3% to +3.9% in August while Byggmax has trailed it by a widening 2.9-6.9 pts for three quarters, so the +5.1% revenue consensus needs a share gap to close that has only widened; a sales miss took the stock -15.7% last October and it ran +5.2% into this print; the gross-margin trend and Clas Ohlson's September partly offset.

Pantheon's revenue budget was cut about 8% between the April and September RNS and nobody has set the two side by side, so the HY NAV probably carries no uplift on 30% of NAV while GBP36p of dividends make a lower NAV-per-share headline plausible; NAV prints have moved this 8%-vol stock under 2.3% every time, and FX, ATC and the buyback offset part of it.

Published Eurex Q3 volumes put Financial Derivatives above a consensus whose range still carries stale pre-September estimates, but the stock sits at a record high, 98% of the mean target and +11% in 20 days with every FY line already modelled above guidance, so a treasury-led raise is the bar and the two roughly cancel; the release is 19:00 CEST so the reaction window is 20 Oct close to 21 Oct close, not the sealed bmo one.

Q3 faces the year's toughest comp (7% organic, P&NO +13%) and the USD 3m net tariff refund that inflated Q2's 22% margin drops out, so a narrowing toward the low end of 5-7% is more likely than the top even though management promised a stronger H2; Ottobock and Enovis read-throughs, and a consensus sitting below Q2's run-rate, pull the other way.

A regulated 9M print inside a reaffirmed guide with a median real-date reaction of 0.82%; the only live line is whether Enagas puts its own 2027 regulated-revenue figure on the final CNMC framework, which the stock did not move on at approval, while the Terega-driven net-debt restatement is arithmetic anyone can do.

The Q3 report is where management promised to quantify Amesto cost synergies, a line no estimate holds, on top of documented Q2 organic and order-intake momentum, in a two-analyst name that is -6% over 20 days; the bar is unsourced and a Swedish IT-consulting sector slowdown report and the Danish drag cap how far that lean goes.

SEK weakness through Q3 adds about a point to reported ARR growth and the y/y comparison is the easiest of the year (Q3-25 added only +9.1 MSEK), both pushing reported ARR to the top of the 10-11% bar on the line this stock moves 5-20% on; against that the CEO's July caution on order intake has been ignored by a 28% rally into the print, which keeps the lean small.

MuM reaffirmed its full-year target in the Q3 release in 2024 and 2025 and missed both, and the 2026 guide needs H2 EBIT up 18-36%, so 'low end' wording or a trim is the live risk on a scheduled first-2027-guide day; the Q2 base effect dropping out gives Q3 EBIT double-digit growth, but that lands inside the guide and the flat tape at 16x shows no belief in the acceleration.

A first FY27 guide on a name that fell 20% and 17% on its last two guide days, after an unexplained 22% slide into the print: September/October price rises of +28-51% on renewals lift the revenue guide mechanically, while a RAM cost index at 604 and an interim CFO make the capex and levered-FCF guide the likely negative; the two are of similar size, so the sign is near even and the move is large either way.

The Q3 EPS bar was raised 15% in 30 days to trend, small beats have been sold intraday on the last two prints, ABG and Lantmannen flag feed-cost pressure for the Q4/2027 outlook and Glenhaven deal costs may put reported EPS below the headline bar; three strategic holders contesting control put a bid under weakness, which is why the lean stays modest.

The first full quarter with zero Aira costs plus the Q3 holiday-pay dip points to EBITDA of 18-20 MSEK (43-47%) against a >35% guide, and margin surprises have been paid (+13.2%, +8.1%) on a stock held at 28-30 SEK for three months; ARR has under-delivered the one analyst twice and Q3 is the slow quarter, and the bar is single-sourced, so the lean is modest.
